senses.definition: from a time in the past until now
senses.explanation: The main clause usually has the present perfect (*have known*, *has been*), because it describes a situation from a past time up to now. The **since** clause usually has the past simple, naming the moment the situation began.

examples.text: I've known her since we were children.
It's been two years since I last saw him.
examples.note: with a length of time before **since**

examples.text: Since he moved to the city, he has been much happier.
Things have changed a lot since you left.

compare.note: **for** gives a length of time (*for two years*); **since** gives the starting point

adaptation.grammar: Many languages use the present tense for a situation that began in the past and continues now. English uses the present perfect in the main clause: *I have lived here since I was ten*, not *I live here since I was ten*.

senses.definition: because; as it is true that
senses.explanation: This **since** gives a reason that the listener probably already knows or will accept easily. It often comes at the start of the sentence.

examples.text: Since you are here, you can help me carry these boxes.
We took a taxi, since it was raining.
Since nobody wanted the last piece, I ate it.

compare.note: **because** puts more weight on the reason, and is the usual answer to **why**

adaptation.semantic: The time sense and the reason sense are expressed by different words in many languages. When the main clause is in the past simple, look at the tense to decide: *since he left* after *has been* is about time; after *we took a taxi* it is about a reason.

learner_errors.incorrect: I live here since I was ten.
learner_errors.correct: I have lived here since I was ten.
learner_errors.note: When **since** gives a starting time, the main clause normally uses the present perfect.

learner_errors.incorrect: Since two years I work here.
learner_errors.correct: I have worked here for two years.
learner_errors.note: Use **for**, not **since**, with a length of time.

see_also.note: without a following clause (*I haven't seen him since*)
